tests.description: Timed check on Selection of Materials and Components

questions.question: Create a simple decision matrix to compare acrylic, polycarbonate and glass for a display cabinet door.
questions.correctAnswer: Criteria with weights: Safety (impact resistance) 5, Transparency 4, Cost 3, Weight 3, Scratch resistance 2. Acrylic: 58. Polycarbonate: 62. Glass: 50. Winner: polycarbonate (best safety and transparency despite higher cost).

questions.question: A designer must choose between aluminium and polypropylene for a kitchen utensil handle. Justify using at least four criteria.
questions.correctAnswer: Function: handle must insulate - PP wins over aluminium. Weight: PP lightweight, aluminium heavier. Cost: PP cheap and easy to mould; aluminium requires die-casting. Durability: aluminium resists staining; PP may stain. Recommendation: PP for budget, aluminium with silicone overmould for premium.

questions.question: Explain how production volume (batch vs mass) influences material selection for a plastic product.
questions.correctAnswer: Mass production (100,000+ units): justifies expensive injection mould tooling - thermoplastics very cheap per unit. Batch (50-500 units): tooling cost per unit too high - use CNC, vacuum forming, or 3D printing.
